findings.claim: Every sidebar section is a root in one flat Seq (treeRoots) projected into one indexed row map, so a long Files subtree pushes every later section, including the package, below the viewport; there is no per-section row budget.
A single scroll offset treeScroll applies to the whole flat list; sections have no scroll state of their own.
The projection places roots in publication order and computes row addresses; the package root is published by PackageSidebar after the Files/Sessions/Agents roots, so it is always below Files.
The package provider's root node is a plain collapsed branch node with the package title, giving it no priority or pinned position in the sidebar.
The viewport height is the screen height minus 4 and the messages panel, shared by all sections; the scroll limit is rows minus that height.

Before the fix the scrollbar was drawn only while the tree was focused (the guard was `treeFocused tree, visible>=3`), so an unfocused sidebar showed no cue that more sections existed; the guard now also accepts any overflow.
Wheel events already scrolled the sidebar by three rows without taking focus, so reachability existed but was undiscoverable.
Key events consult the compiled keybindings first; only unbound keys reach the hard-coded treeKey, so Home/End/Ctrl+Down did nothing in a live sidebar until they became bindable sidebar commands.

limitations: Only the remote display protocol path was exercised; native window, web and terminal frontends were built disabled (-f-window -f-web -f-terminal).
HLS on hide itself did not work, so no definitions or references were followed through HLS.
The full editor-tests suite (SidebarCheck, BindingsCheck, ProtocolCheck, AccessibilityCheck) was not run; it covers code touched by this change.
No per-frame allocation baseline was measured; added render work is bounded to about 33 ordered-map lookups per frame while the tree overflows.
The accessibility tree does not announce the new cue.
The sandbox has about 2 GB RAM; compiling Hide.Model needs most of it, so builds must run with no concurrent editor session.
